evidence: Receiving DO2 drops from ~12.1 (48.0h) to 7.75 (48.2h) and declines to 6.94 mg/L at 52.0h
Source batches at 52h show DO2 ~10.5-11 mg/L, ~4 mg/L higher than receiving at same age
Receiving P(48h)=2.82 g/L, consistent with active production phase needing adequate oxygen
DO2 minimum constraint is 2.0 mg/L; extrapolated declining trend poses risk under KEEP
increase_air is bounded [1.0, 1.15] and preserves feed, hence product mass, unlike reduce_feed/stop
submission.rationale: Receiving fermentation shows a clear oxygen-supply deficit emerging at 48.2h: DO2 fell abruptly to ~7.75 mg/L and declined steadily to 6.94 mg/L by 52h, about 4 mg/L below comparable source batches at the same age (10.5-11 mg/L). This sustained downward trend indicates receiving oxygen demand exceeds current aeration, risking approach to the 2.0 mg/L minimum and slowing production (P(48h)=2.82 g/L already slightly below source trajectory). increase_air directly raises oxygen transfer with no loss of feed or product mass, unlike feed reductions, and is a bounded, reversible intervention.
submission.uncertainty: No direct OUR or kLa measurements; the abrupt DO2 step at 48.2h could partly be sensor-related, though the consistent 4h decline across many samples supports a real trend. Product assays lag 4h, so early impact on productivity can't be confirmed immediately. If aeration headroom is already saturated, increase_air may under-deliver and combined action would be the fallback.

evidence: Receiving DO2 step-down at t=48.2h: 12.10 -> 7.75 mg/L, continuing drift to 6.94 mg/L at t=52h
Source batches at t=48-52h show DO2 ~10.5-11.3 mg/L; no equivalent dip — receiving-specific transfer anomaly
Receiving P assay at t=48h (avail. 52h): 2.82 g/L, on track vs source 2.98-3.06 g/L
Forward model update: estimated oxygen transfer multiplier 0.632 with change at t=48h
Forward model predictions: combined = 598 kg, min DO 3.19, 5/5 sensitivity members feasible; keep = 284 kg, min DO 2.49, 4/5 feasible; increase_air min DO 2.38 (4/5); reduce_feed min DO 2.83 (4/5)
submission.rationale: At t=48 h the receiving DO2 stepped down from ~12.1 to ~7.7 mg/L and continues to fall (6.94 mg/L at t=52 h), while all three source batches at the same age hold ~10-11 mg/L — indicating a receiving-specific oxygen transfer impairment (forward model estimates transfer multiplier dropped to ~0.63). Product is on track (2.82 g/L at 48 h vs ~3.0 g/L source), so this is an oxygen-capacity fault, not a production failure. Source-calibrated forward model: keep gives 284 kg with post-decision min DO 2.49 mg/L and sensitivity members down to 1.8 (oxygen-constraint risk); increase_air (315 kg, min DO 2.38) and reduce_feed (340 kg, min DO 2.83) each leave sensitivity members near/below the 2.0 mg/L limit; combined (0.8 feed, 1.15 air) gives 598 kg product with min DO 3.19 mg/L and all 5 sensitivity members feasible. Combined therefore both restores oxygen margin and preserves/increases product mass, and avoids a stop (which would count zero production).
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is nominal and source-calibrated, not the hidden realization; actual transfer impairment and kinetics may differ. If the DO2 dip were partly a sensor artifact, combined would still be safe (retains feed, only +15% air). If the transfer fault worsens beyond the modeled 0.63 multiplier, min DO2 could approach the 2.0 mg/L limit and a stronger action might be needed. Product mass gains from combined rely on model extrapolation; observed data alone only confirm the DO2 deficit and on-track product at 48 h.
